newsitem.title: ABU DHABI: UAE says ready for talks with Iran on islands' row.
newsitem.headline: UAE says ready for talks with Iran on islands' row.

text.p: The United Arab Emirates said it was ready for immediate talks with Iran on three disputed Gulf islands, a row that had strained ties between the two oil-rich countries.

The official Emirates news agency WAM said late on Wednesday the UAE "expressed its full readiness to conduct immediate contacts with Iran to ascertain the Islamic republic's readiness to discuss and make necessary arrangements for negotiations ... on the three islands of Abu Musa and Greater and Lesser Tunbs."

"In the case such negotiations fail to solve the dispute, the two sides should agree to refer the issue to the International Court of Justice," WAM quoted an official source at the Foreign Ministry as saying.
WAM said the official was reacting to comments on May 25 by Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Iran's readiness to negotiate the dispute.

Iran's president-elect Mohammad Khatami, who will take over from Rafsanjani in August, said on Tuesday the three islands belonged to Iran, but urged bilateral negotiations to settle the territorial dispute.

Since 1992 Iran and the UAE have been at loggerheads over the islands that are close to key oil shipping lanes at the mouth of the Gulf. Gulf Arab states have long demanded an end to Iranian "occupation" of the islands.
Abu Dhabi has urged Tehran to agree to take the dispute to the International Court of Justice in The Hague. But Iran has said the row should be settled through negotiations.
The Tehran government has repeatedly said the islands were "inseparable parts of Iran".
The UAE last year accused Iran of deploying offensive weapons at the three disputed islands.
